title: Bounded-Degree Equations in Rasta and Dasta Attacks
summary: More complicated equations can reduce attack data while leaving linearization time and memory unchanged, but their bounded-degree count and maximum achievable data reduction remain unknown.

formal_statement.body: For the Rasta and Dasta attacks, more complicated exploitable equations constructed from a plaintext-ciphertext pair can reduce data complexity, while the time and memory complexity of the linearization attack remain unchanged. The unresolved problem is to characterize or upper-bound, for each prescribed maximum degree, the number of exploitable equations of degree at most that bound and to determine the greatest reduction in data complexity achievable from them; the available evidence only indicates that this number appears small and that the data complexity may not be significantly reduced.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of Rasta and Dasta using exploitable low-degree equations and linearization attacks.
parameters: Maximum equation degree: bounds the degrees of exploitable equations included in the count
Number of exploitable equations: the degree-bounded quantity to characterize or upper-bound
Data-complexity reduction: the achievable attack improvement to determine
scope.unresolved_remainder: For each prescribed maximum degree, characterize or upper-bound the number of exploitable equations and determine the greatest resulting reduction in data complexity.

citations.label: Algebraic Attacks on Rasta and Dasta Using Low-Degree Equations

progress.summary: The source reports that constructing more complicated equations from a plaintext-ciphertext pair can reduce data complexity without changing linearization time or memory. It indicates that the bounded-degree equation count appears small but leaves both that count and the attainable reduction unresolved.
